svg.aria-label: Most common owner complaints about wireless earbuds, ranked qualitatively

g.text: What earbud owners complain about most (recent 1–3★ reviews and owner threads)
Occasional
Common
Very common
Fit: falling out, pressure, pain after an hour
The #1 reason for returns. Ear shapes vary more than earbuds do; foam tips and a fit test fix most cases, hook designs fix the rest.
Battery fades after 12–24 months
Tiny non-replaceable cells; heat and full-charge storage accelerate it. Expect 60–70% of day-one runtime by year two on any brand.
Connection dropouts, stutter, one side cutting out
Crowded 2.4 GHz areas, phone in a back pocket, multipoint fighting over two devices. Firmware updates fix a surprising share.
One earbud won't charge / case won't charge
Usually dirty charging contacts (ear wax + sweat) — not a defect. Clean pins with a dry swab before claiming warranty.
ANC: pressure feeling, hiss, wind noise
Pressure sensitivity is individual; try a lower ANC level or adaptive mode. Some AirPods Pro 3 owners reported static that firmware addressed.
Touch controls too sensitive or unresponsive
Stem-squeeze (Apple, Nothing, Beats) draws far fewer complaints than touch pads (Samsung, Sony, budget brands).
Call quality in wind, traffic, or a busy office
Bose, Sony XM6 and AirPods lead the labs; Technics, Sennheiser and most budget buds trail. If you take calls outdoors, weight this heavily.
Counterfeits and "renewed" units sold as new
Mostly AirPods. Buy "Ships from and sold by Amazon.com" or Apple/Best Buy, and check Find My + separate L/R serials on arrival.
Qualitative ranking of themes across recent Amazon 1–3★ reviews and Reddit owner threads for the earbuds in this guide — a tally, not a survey.
